title: Beads work on its own board
eyebrow: The move ran; three things are named and left standing

questions.ask: 109 cards still carry the board tag on the racing board. They are that project's own job machinery — the tool that pours a card, the gates, the standard a ticket is held to. Do they move too?

options.label: Leave them where they are
options.detail: They govern the racing project and can only be enforced from inside it; the shared-machinery job will lift them out properly, board and all.

options.label: Move them to the beads board now
options.detail: Every board-tagged card ends up in one place, as you first asked — but the gates that police them go on running from the racing project, so a card and the thing it fixes sit on opposite sides.

content.label: What happened
content.lead: Work about the beads app now lives on the beads board, and the racing board is that much lighter.

rows: Beads-app work sitting on the racing board
Whole families moved with their children intact

items: Every card was checked after it landed: title, wording, what it is judged by, priority, both tags, and its place in its family.
One card was moved and checked on its own before any of the rest followed.
Both boards were photographed before anything moved, so any of it can be put back.

content.label: The rule used to split them
content.lead: A card belongs to the board of the checkout whose files it changes.

items: Work on the beads app's own screen moved here.
Work on the racing project's job machinery stayed there, because it governs only that project and can only be enforced from inside it.
Eleven cards could honestly have gone either way: four came here, seven stayed.

content.label: What is left standing, and why
content.lead: Three remainders, each with a card of its own rather than a note in someone's head.

rows: You have sessions working on their parents right now, and pulling a card out from under a working session breaks it
Its own card, to finish in a quiet moment

Two rules eat each other: the reader must find nothing left to answer before it lets go, and every answer it writes is refused for how it is worded, so it can never finish. Their copies here are already correct and in place
Joined to the shared-machinery job, now building
The tool that pours a card
It is wired to the racing project with no way to point it elsewhere, which is why this board could only borrow it by hand

decisions.title: Cards go by the checkout they change, not by their tag
decisions.why: Moving the whole tag would have dragged the racing project's own machinery onto a board that does not govern it, where none of its gates could reach it.

decisions.title: Both boards photographed before anything moved
decisions.why: Retiring dozens of cards across two live boards is one-way; a bad batch had to be recoverable.

decisions.title: One card moved and checked alone before the rest
decisions.why: The path this board uses to make cards is borrowed and fragile, so it was proved on one before it was trusted with sixty.

decisions.title: Finished and cancelled history stayed where it happened
decisions.why: It is a record of what was done in that project; dragging it across would make the new board read as older than it is.

decisions.title: Two cards were retired rather than moved
decisions.why: They asked for the very thing the chat work already covers, so moving them would have put the same job on the board twice.

decisions.title: The three stuck retirements were not forced by hand
decisions.why: The board refuses to let the session holding a job wave its own reading through, and that refusal is the whole value of the reading; the gap it exposes belongs to the shared-machinery job, not to a hand-made exception.

next.if_nothing: The beads board is the one to work from for anything about the app; the ten cards still on the racing board stay reachable and nothing is lost.
